information.description:
Agents and Executioners are cut from the same cloth, that of freelance mercs whom ‘saka liked so well got a full-time contract. They’re usually sent on assassination or sabotage jobs that don’t require much stealth, and have more than enough chrome to succeed. The only real difference between Agents and Executioners is just what they like to call themselves, since at the end of the day they do the same thing — pull the corp’s trigger.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Arasaka).

A cybernetical replacement arm. Comes with a free hand.
Requires cyberarm. The cyberarm this is installed on cannot be broken.

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 7 (2d6)

Hormone regulation implant designed to improve the user’s fight or flight response. Induces a powerful adrenaline rush on command.

Neuralware. As an Action, the user may activate this cyberware, after which it remains active for the next 60 seconds (20 Rounds). While Berserk is active, the user ignores the penalties (excluding the auto Critical Injury effect) of the Seriously and Mortally Wounded wound states. Mortally Wounded users must still make Death Saves. This cyberware has a 1 hour cooldown before it can be activated again.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • The wound-state penalties the sheet applies can't be switched off per item; ignore them by hand while Berserk is active.

Run the edge at top speed, choomba. There ain’t another way to live.

Speedware. As an Action, the user may activate this cyberware, after which it remains active for the next 60 seconds (20 Rounds). While active, this cyberware provides a +3 bonus to any Initiative Roll made. If activated while the user is already in an Initiative Queue, their current Initiative increases by 3, which is lost if this cyberware deactivates or its duration expires during combat. This cyberware has a 1 hour cooldown before it can be activated again. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Clinic
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Sandevistan; use this one instead of the core item.
  • Matches the core item's setup: the +3 shows as a toggle in the initiative roll dialog.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive)

Sensors and coprocessors that overclock speedware in emergencies.

Sandevistan Cyberware Enhancement. When a perceived hostile target that is within 6m/yds of the user activates Speedware, or has active Speedware when Initiative is rolled, the user may activate their Sandevistan without an Action. When done, Sandevistan’s Initiative Bonus is increased by 2 (+5 Total), but is only active for the next 9 seconds (3 Rounds). An SOS-triggered Sandevistan has triple its usual cooldown time before it can be activated again.

Enhances: Sandevistan
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • Change the Sandevistan's initiative effect to +5 by hand when it fires through SOS.
